plan: With 3 bidders total (including myself) and the ascending clock mechanism where the sealed bid acts as an automatic exit point, this functions like a second-price auction. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, so bidding my true value of $24 ensures I only win when profitable and never overpay relative to my value.

Since the sealed bid acts as an exit price in an ascending clock auction (effectively a second-price mechanism), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever the price is below my value and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down since overbidding risks negative profit and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the ascending clock will end at the second-highest sealed bid, and I pay that price if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $24 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid price, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.
